note: Misses four of five criteria and is the clearest out-of-ICP call in this batch. 'successful' fails on the ICP's own wording — he is a 25-year-old underground miner about two years into the role, not a business owner, physician or equivalent, and he frames himself as early-career: 'I'm still pretty early on in my career.' 'income' fails outright and verifiably; he did the arithmetic himself and concluded 'in my current financial state, it is impossible', with the discounted tier costing close to a month of post-tax pay. 'neglected_health' fails because health is not a neglected corner of an otherwise sorted life — 'I've always been overweight my entire life' and 'I've lived most of my entire life pretty much being relatively unhealthy.' 'good_to_great' fails for the same reason; this is rescue, and he says so, describing needing 'a clean bill of health' and 'the basics and the fundamentals' before he can attempt a beginner bouldering route. 'not_deconditioned' is the one match and it is a real one: at roughly 95 kg and 5'10" he is about 10 kg over his own target rather than the 50 lb the exclusion describes, he trains with a PT, he works twelve-hour physical shifts, and he is emphatically not gym-averse — he is dissatisfied with the gym he has. The finding is upstream of the closer: this prospect was booked into a 76-minute closer call believing the programme was free, which means nothing in the setter stage tested either the ICP criteria or the price. He is also the second data point after Badrane Hriouch that 'income' is the criterion the funnel actually fails on.
